subject: Follow-up: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — feature parity & next tests
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@edgeai.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@edgeai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — feature parity & next tests

Samir / Lena,

Thanks again for carving out time this morning — good conversation and helpful signal on where EdgeAI will focus the evaluation. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next-steps slate so we can turn this into a concrete PoC: 

What we heard (high level)
- Primary use case: real-time inference across multimodal prompts for customer-facing workflows.
- Current evaluation targets: AWS Bedrock (Aurora/Anthropic), Google Vertex/PaLM, and in-house on-prem stacks.
- Must-haves for your team: deterministic structured outputs for billing/records, dependable tool/function-calling for downstream systems, and streaming low-latency partial responses for live UI.

Redwood differentiators called out on the call
- Function/tool calling: explicit structured tool-call objects + opt-in blocking/non-blocking call modes (we can capture success/failure rates and enforce schemas).
- Structured outputs: built-in schema enforcement + automatic JSON reify/fallback when the model drifts; we include schema mismatch logs for debugging.
- Streaming: partial token streaming with latency SLOs and incremental JSON assembly; we expose p50/p95 metrics per stream and can abort/rollback partial outputs if an error occurs.
- Cost controls: prefix caching and workload-aware batching to reduce token costs without blowing latency for your 200ms SLOs.

Proposed PoC scope & tests (please confirm or edit)
1) Function / tool-calling fidelity (owner: Neha)
   - 500 synthetic prompts that should trigger 3 different tool calls (lookup, charge_authorize, open_ticket).
   - Accept if tool-call success >= 98% and schema-conformance >= 99% for the returned objects.

2) Structured-output validation (owner: Marcus)
   - Run 1k prompts with target JSON schema (invoice/charge records); measure schema pass rate, and common drift categories.
   - Acceptance: >= 99% well-formed JSON, <= 2% critical-field errors.

3) Streaming & latency (owner: Rishi)
   - Simulate 50 concurrent users, 5 RPS each, measure token-to-first-byte and tail latencies (p95/p99).
   - Acceptance: median token-first-byte < 120ms; p95 < 400ms for light models.

4) Comparative run vs hyperscaler endpoints (owner: Marcus)
   - Same prompts run against Bedrock/Vertex and Redwood-hosted model variants; capture QoQ cost, latency, and pass rates.
   - We'll provide a feature matrix and runbook (attached).

Deliverables & timeline
- Kickoff and credentials exchange: within 3 business days after your go-ahead.
- Test runs (week 1): function-calling + structured output sanity checks.
- Comparative runs (week 2): streaming and cost/throughput sweeps.
- Results deck and recommended next actions (end of week 3).

Attachments: redwood_feature_matrix.xlsx (feature parity snapshot)

Ask from you
- Confirm: test scope above + any additional security/compliance checks (e.g., SOC2 evidence) you need included in the PoC.
- Point of contact for engineering credentials (service account or temporary API key) and preferred cloud endpoints to compare.

If that plan looks good, we'll get the PoC runbook and a short checklist over to you today so your infra team can establish keys.

Thanks — looking forward to running the tests.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions 
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_feature_matrix.xlsx (Spreadsheet, 240KB)]

From: Samir Shah <samir@edgeai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@edgeai.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:20:13 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — feature parity & next tests

Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. This looks like the right shape. A couple of quick notes/questions from EdgeAI before we lock timelines: 

1) Security/compliance: we will need SOC2/ISO evidence for any private deployment. Can you surface a minimal evidence pack and a simple statement of data residency guarantees for the PoC?
2) Benchmarks: when you say "compare vs hyperscalers", we specifically want to benchmark against Bedrock (Anthropic + Claude variants) and Vertex (PaLM-family). Can you include those endpoints in the runbook?
3) Demo env: can you create a short-lived keyed environment for us (non-prod) so we don't touch our production keys? Ideally an API key with a usage cap.

Also, curious on an implementation detail: for function-calling, what's your strategy when a tool-call fails (model returns malformed args)? We noticed other vendors either return an error token that bubbles to the client or they auto-retry with a different prompt. Which approach will Redwood use for the PoC by default?

If you can answer those and provision a test key we can target a kickoff early next week.

—Samir
Samir Shah
VP Product, EdgeAI
[External]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@edgeai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — feature parity & next tests

Hi Samir — appreciate the questions. Quick answers and executable next-step items below.

On compliance evidence:
- We'll share a SOC2 summary + evidence checklist (redacted) in the PoC folder. For the PoC, we provide encrypted logs and a commitment to retain only request metadata unless otherwise requested.

On including hyperscaler endpoints:
- Yes — we'll include Bedrock and Vertex targets in the runbook. We'll keep the request shapes identical and surface call-level metrics so you can compare model + infra differences.

Function-calling failure modes & default behavior (PoC)
- Default: return a structured tool-call error object and do NOT auto-retry. Rationale: deterministic handling and observable failure signals are critical for downstream systems.
- Optional mode: a limited automatic repair attempt (single-shot few-shot correction) that can be enabled for tolerant flows; we'll document expected FP/TP tradeoffs.

Concrete owners & acceptance criteria (short)
- Function-calling (Neha): produce runbook, 500 prompts, measure call-success and schema-conformance. Deliverable: CSV of calls + top 10 failure buckets.
- Structured outputs (Marcus): 1k runs, JSON schema validator results, sample bad-output audits.
- Streaming & perf (Rishi): playback harness + p50/p95/p99 reports, token-first-byte latency.

Runbook & access
- I'll drop the PoC instructions in the shared Drive and provision a short-lived API key (scoped to PoC) once we confirm timeline.
- Temporary key policy: 7-day TTL, billing capped, request-level logging enabled.

Timeline proposal (firm)
- Thu Feb 12: confirm PoC kickoff and approve the non-prod key.
- Mon Feb 16–Fri Feb 20: test execution.
- Fri Feb 27: results review + next-step decision.

Attaching the PoC runbook PDF and the feature matrix that Marcus already referenced.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: poC-instructions.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]
